clauses.reason: Terminated by express supersession. EO 8384 (Franklin D. Roosevelt, signed March 29, 1940), section 21, states "This order shall supersede" and lists, over a line break, Executive Orders No. 7845 of March 21, 1938, No. 7879 of May 9, 1938, and No. 8226 of August 24, 1939, and states that it "shall be effective as of March 2, 1940". The held text names EO 8226 with its number and date. The end is recorded at the stated effective date, 1940-03-02, which precedes the signing date; the signing date, 1940-03-29, is the alternative reading. Section 15 of EO 8384 restates the same temporary-employee leave rule, so the rule continues under the later order.

conflict_resolutions.EVENT_BEFORE_SIGNING: The 1938-03-21 supersession edge is the Office of the Federal Register record of EO 7845 superseding EO 7409. It is attached to EO 7845, the parent that EO 8226 amends, and is not an event of EO 8226, which was signed 1939-08-24. The first end of EO 8226 is the supersession by EO 8384.

research_rationale:
EO 8226 of August 24, 1939 (Franklin D. Roosevelt; Federal Register of August 26, 1939, held text), Amending Section 15 of Executive Order No. 7845 of March 21, 1938, Prescribing Regulations Relating to Annual Leave of Government Employees. Identity: number, date and subject agree with the census register row. The order amends section 15 of EO 7845 to read as set out in the order: temporary employees who receive indefinite, emergency, probational or permanent appointments in the same department or agency without break in service are entitled to annual leave for each full month of service to the date of appointment and are credited with accrued leave. It states "This order shall be effective as of June 30, 1939" with publication in the Federal Register (the held text prints "effective as of June 30, 1939" across a line break, so the phrase is paraphrased here). The order has no term of its own. First end: EO 8384 of March 29, 1940 (5 FR 1253, Federal Register of April 2, 1940), whose section 21 begins "This order shall supersede" and continues, over a line break, with the list Executive Orders No. 7845 of March 21, 1938, No. 7879 of May 9, 1938, and No. 8226 of August 24, 1939, and states that it "shall be effective as of March 2, 1940" (sections 6 and 9 excepted, effective as of July 1, 1936). This is an express supersession of the whole order, not an amendment. Date reading: the end is recorded at the stated effective date, 1940-03-02, which precedes the signing date; the alternative reading is the signing date, 1940-03-29, for a reviewer who treats the retroactive date as not governing. Search: a by-number search of the held order texts returns no match for the number 8226 in the 'Executive Order No. 8226' form; EO 8384 was found through the later-events chain (the Office of the Federal Register note 'Revoked by: EO 8384, March 29, 1940') and confirmed by reading its section 21. Searches: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts) were chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no scope warning.

savings.reason: The substance of EO 8226 continues in the superseding order: section 15 of EO 8384 carries the same rule that temporary employees who "subsequently receive indefinite," emergency, probational or permanent appointments in the same department or agency without a break in service are entitled to annual leave for each full month and are credited with accrued leave. Leave earned under EO 8226 between June 30, 1939 and March 2, 1940 is an accrued effect; the held EO 8384 text provides for adjustment of leave on the basis of its regulations in section 21 and no held source shows any loss of leave earned under EO 8226.
